sections.title: Header — every setting
sections.excerpt: Header — every setting | The top bar of the screen — the Back and Skip buttons and the progress indicator that shows how far along the visitor is. This guide documents every setting of the Header block, grouped by area. Each setting matches a real control in the screen editor.

sections.title: Header Bar Background
sections.excerpt: Header Bar Background | Fills the header bar with a color, or clear it to transparent so the screen background shows through for a floating header. Use a solid color to set the header apart from busy content. If you go transparent over a photo or video, check that the Back, Skip, and progress colors still stand out clearly.

sections.title: Header Bar Height
sections.excerpt: Header Bar Height | Sets how tall the header bar is, from 20 to 200 pixels, with a default of 44, which is the space its buttons and progress bar share. Keep it near the default for a standard bar and raise it only if you add a tall icon or larger text. Going too small cramps the Back and Skip buttons and makes them hard to tap.

sections.title: Header See-Through Level
sections.excerpt: Header See-Through Level | Fades the whole header bar from fully solid to fully see-through, defaulting to solid. Lower it for a soft, partly transparent header that blends into a photo or video background. Keep it high enough that the Back, Skip, and progress controls stay easy to see.

sections.title: Back Button Label
sections.excerpt: Back Button Label | Sets the text and styling of the Back control that returns visitors to the previous step. Defaults to a left arrow and supports other languages. Keep it small so it doesn't compete with your main action, and clear it to hide the button on the first screen, where there's nowhere to go back to.

sections.title: Back button text style
sections.excerpt: Back button text style | Overrides how the Back control's label looks — font, size, weight, color, alignment, line height, an optional highlight behind the text, and a strikethrough color. By default it inherits your project theme, which keeps every screen consistent. Touch this only when the Back label needs to match a specific header treatment, and keep it subtle so it never competes with your main action.

sections.title: Spacing inside the header
sections.excerpt: Spacing inside the header | Sets the inner spacing on each side (top, right, bottom, left) that pushes the Back button, Skip button, and progress bar away from the header edges. Raise the top value to keep these controls clear of the phone's status bar or notch, and adjust left/right so buttons aren't jammed against the screen edge. Start from the defaults and nudge only where something looks cramped, since a clean header keeps the first impression of your ad landing page tidy.

sections.title: Completed Progress Color
sections.excerpt: Completed Progress Color | Colors the filled, completed part of the progress bar. Defaults to gold for the Line style and teal for Dashes. Use your brand accent and make sure it clearly stands out against the unfilled track color so visitors can see at a glance how far they've come.

sections.title: Progress Content Side
sections.excerpt: Progress Content Side | Sets where the icon and label sit across the header, on the left (Start), centered, or on the right (End). Mostly a cosmetic touch: centered usually looks balanced, while left or right lets you line the label up with your Back or Skip button. Adjust only if the default looks off.

sections.title: Optional Header Icon
sections.excerpt: Optional Header Icon | Adds an optional small icon, often a logo or step glyph, next to the progress bar, with controls for the image, its size, and its spacing. Most funnels leave this off. Use it only to reinforce branding in the header, and keep the icon small so it doesn't crowd the progress bar.

sections.title: Header icon settings
sections.excerpt: Header icon settings | Controls the optional header icon shown next to the progress bar — its image (upload or URL), placement relative to the label, scale mode, width, height, corner rounding, and padding. Off by default. Turn it on only to reinforce branding in the header, and keep the icon small so it doesn't crowd the progress bar or the Back and Skip buttons.

sections.title: Progress Bar Style
sections.excerpt: Progress Bar Style | Chooses how progress through the funnel looks: a single continuous bar (Line) or segmented dots (Dashes), each with its own color controls below. A visible 'how far along' cue reassures visitors only a few steps remain, which lifts completion. Pick whichever fits your brand and keep it the same across screens.

sections.title: Keep Progress Clear Of Buttons
sections.excerpt: Keep Progress Clear Of Buttons | When on, which is the default, the progress bar shrinks so it never overlaps the Back or Skip buttons; when off, it can collide with them in a tight header. Leave it on. Turn it off only if you've removed those buttons and want the bar to use the full width.

sections.title: Progress Bar Text
sections.excerpt: Progress Bar Text | Optional text shown with the progress bar, such as a 'Step 5 of 10' counter or a short line of reassurance. Supports other languages and styling; leave it empty for a clean bar-only look. Note this text is fixed per screen and won't count up on its own, so use it as a label unless you drive it from a variable.

sections.title: Progress text style
sections.excerpt: Progress text style | Overrides how the progress label (for example 'Step 5 of 10') looks — font, size, weight, color, alignment, line height, an optional highlight, and a strikethrough color. By default it inherits your theme. Use it to make the reassurance text legible against your header background, and keep it small so it supports rather than overshadows the progress bar.

sections.title: Remaining Progress Color
sections.excerpt: Remaining Progress Color | Colors the empty, not-yet-completed part of the progress bar. Defaults to white for the Line style and light gray for Dashes. Keep it muted next to the filled color so the completed portion clearly reads as progress rather than blending in.

sections.title: Stretch Progress Edge-To-Edge
sections.excerpt: Stretch Progress Edge-To-Edge | When on, the progress bar stretches all the way across the header; when off, it takes only the width its content needs. Use full width for a bold, obvious progress bar across the top of the screen. Turn it off when you want the bar compact and grouped with a label or icon.

sections.title: Spacing around the progress bar
sections.excerpt: Spacing around the progress bar | Sets the spacing on each side of the progress indicator alone, separate from the header's overall padding. Use it to fine-tune the gap around the bar, for example to nudge it down from the buttons, without moving the buttons themselves. Most funnels keep the default; adjust only when the bar sits too tight or too loose against the header.

sections.title: Progress Height In Header
sections.excerpt: Progress Height In Header | Sets where the progress bar sits up and down within the header: at the top, centered, or at the bottom. Centered is the usual balanced choice; use bottom to sit it just above your content, or top to hug the status bar. Adjust only if the default placement looks off for your header height.

sections.title: Skip Button Label
sections.excerpt: Skip Button Label | Sets the text and styling of the Skip control that lets visitors bypass this step. Defaults to 'SKIP' and supports other languages. Use it only where skipping is fine, and clear it to hide it on your paywall and key question screens, where an easy out lowers both sales and the answers you collect.

sections.title: Skip button text style
sections.excerpt: Skip button text style | Overrides how the Skip control's label looks — font, size, weight, color, alignment, line height, an optional highlight, and a strikethrough color. By default it inherits your theme. Keep Skip visually quiet (smaller, lower-contrast) so it doesn't pull attention away from continuing; restyle it only to fit a specific header look.
